pull.title: feat(api): serve OpenAI Chat Completions, and refuse to serve an unauthenticated proxy to the network
pull.body:
## What this is

MCC accepted three inbound shapes and none of them was the one almost every
OpenAI-compatible client actually sends. Cline, Aider, Goose, Droid and every
IDE plugin that says "point me at an OpenAI base URL" speak
`POST /v1/chat/completions`; MCC answered 404. This adds that surface, and fixes
the auth fail-open (§63F) in the same release because both are about who can
reach this proxy and on what terms.

`POST /v1/chat/completions` sits beside `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` and
is built the way the Responses adapter was: a `core` package that only
translates, and a handler that hands the result to the same `ModelRouter` ->
`ProviderExecutor` every other surface uses. Routing, fallback, pause, reasoning
gating, output budgets, wire capture, the upstream ladder, the request log,
analytics and the optimizer rules therefore apply to all three doors
identically.

## Request translation (Chat Completions -> MessagesRequest)

| Client field | Anthropic |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | `model` (the same refs the other two accept, through the existing resolver) |
| `messages[system\|developer].content` | `system`, joined with a blank line |
| `messages[user].content` string | `content` string |
| `messages[user].content` parts | `text` blocks; `image_url` -> `image` with a `base64` source for a data URL, a `url` source for http |
| `messages[assistant].content` | assistant `text` block (dropped when empty and only tool calls remain) |
| `messages[assistant].tool_calls[]` | `tool_use` blocks, arguments JSON-decoded |
| `messages[assistant].reasoning_content` | `Message.reasoning_content` |
| `messages[tool]` | `tool_result` blocks; consecutive ones coalesce into **one** user turn |
| `max_completion_tokens` / `max_tokens` | `max_tokens` (the newer field wins when both are sent) |
| `temperature`, `top_p` | same |
| `stop` (string or list) | `stop_sequences` |
| `tools[].function` | `tools[]` `{name, description, input_schema}` |
| `tool_choice` `auto`/`none`/`required`/`{type:function}` | omitted / tools withheld / `{"type":"any"}` / `{"type":"tool","name":…}` |
| `parallel_tool_calls: false` | `tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use` (built even with no `tool_choice`) |
| `reasoning_effort` | `output_config: {"effort": …}` — the name travels, routing prices it |
| `response_format` `json_object` / `json_schema` | a system instruction; `json_schema` carries its schema verbatim |
| `metadata`, `user` | `metadata` (+ `metadata.user_id`) |
| `stream` | recorded as the client's intent; the internal request is always `stream: true` |
| `n` > 1 | **400** `invalid_request_error`, `param: "n"` |
| `seed`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty` | dropped, with one trace row naming them |
| unknown `response_format.type`, non-function tool, unknown role | **400** naming the value |

## Stream translation (Anthropic SSE -> chat.completion.chunk)

| Anthropic event | Chunk |
| --- | --- |
| `message_start` | first chunk, `delta: {role:"assistant", content:""}`; seeds prompt/cache counts |
| `content_block_delta` `text_delta` | `delta.content` |
| `content_block_start`/`delta` `thinking` | `delta.reasoning_content` **and** `delta.reasoning` (same text) |
| `content_block_start` `tool_use` | `delta.tool_calls[{index, id, type:"function", function:{name, arguments:""}}]` |
| `input_json_delta` | `delta.tool_calls[{index, function:{arguments: fragment}}]` |
| `message_delta.stop_reason` | `end_turn`/`stop_sequence` -> `stop`, `max_tokens` -> `length`, `tool_use` -> `tool_calls` |
| `message_stop` | finish chunk (`delta: {}`), then the usage chunk, then `data: [DONE]` |
| `error`, or a failure after the first frame | `data: {"error":{…}}` then `[DONE]` — what the OpenAI SDK stream readers raise on |

The tool-call index is **not** the Anthropic block index: a reply whose first
block is text and whose next two are tool calls streams as tool-call 0 and 1.
`stream_options.include_usage` appends one choiceless chunk carrying
`prompt_tokens` (including cache reads), `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`,
`prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and a capped
`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`.

Non-streaming assembles that same internal stream into one `chat.completion` at
the API boundary, the way `/v1/messages` already does. There is no second
pipeline to drift.

## The auth decision

Both options were investigated.

- **First-run flow.** `mcc-init` writes `.env.example` into `~/.fcc/.env`, and
  that template sets `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="freecc"`. The admin manifest offers
  the same default. `mcc-server` never creates a `.env` itself. So a fresh
  install always has a token and a startup refusal cannot break first run —
  pinned by `test_the_shipped_defaults_start_without_a_refusal`.
- **Generating a token on first run** would silently break every client already
  configured to send nothing, and would have to be written into the managed
  `.env` on a path that today has no reason to write there.

So: **refuse to start**, in `cli/commands.py::_run_supervised_server`, before
`uvicorn.Config` and before the port probe. The policy itself is
`config/proxy_auth.open_proxy_without_auth_error`. The compare in
`require_proxy_auth` is untouched. Loopback binds with no token still run.

Live, on the scratch server:

```
$ HOST=0.0.0.0 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN= mcc-server
Refusing to start: HOST is '0.0.0.0', which accepts connections from other
machines, and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is empty, so this proxy would serve anyone
who can reach it. Set ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN to a secret, or set HOST=127.0.0.1
to serve this machine only (change either on the dashboard under
Providers -> Runtime).
EXIT=1

$ HOST=127.0.0.1 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN= mcc-server
health: 200
POST /v1/chat/completions (no Authorization header) -> 200
```

The page and card the message names are read back out of the shipped `admin.js`
and the admin manifest by `tests/contracts/test_proxy_auth_startup_policy.py`,
so renaming either fails a check rather than a user's search.

## Live proof — the real OpenAI Python SDK (2.54.0) against MCC on 127.0.0.1:8199

Upstream is a fake OpenAI-compatible gateway on 8299 reached through the
`lmstudio` provider, so the whole chain is exercised: client Chat Completions ->
Anthropic internal -> executor -> upstream OpenAI chat -> Anthropic SSE ->
Chat Completions SSE.

```
1. GET /v1/models through the SDK
10 model ids; first 5: ['anthropic/lmstudio/fake-model',
 'claude-3-freecc-no-thinking/lmstudio/fake-model', 'claude-fable-5',
 'claude-opus-4-20250514', 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514']

2. Non-streaming chat.completions.create
id            : chatcmpl-e2e4b9c21cee446dbd1401cdadfb672a
object        : chat.completion
model         : lmstudio/fake-model
finish_reason : stop
content       : Hello from the fake gateway.
usage         : {'completion_tokens': 17, 'prompt_tokens': 41, 'total_tokens': 58,
                 'prompt_tokens_details': {'cached_tokens': 12}}

3. Streaming with stream_options.include_usage
finish_reason : stop
id            : chatcmpl-f281d149314d4320a9d47401d96f359f
streamed text : Hello from the fake gateway.
usage         : {'completion_tokens': 17, 'prompt_tokens': 41, 'total_tokens': 58,
                 'prompt_tokens_details': {'cached_tokens': 12}}

4. Streaming reasoning_effort -> delta.reasoning_content
reasoning_content: Let me think about that. Two plus two.
content          : The answer is 4.
usage            : {'completion_tokens': 17, 'prompt_tokens': 41, 'total_tokens': 58,
                    'completion_tokens_details': {'reasoning_tokens': 11},
                    'prompt_tokens_details': {'cached_tokens': 12}}

5. Tool call round trip
finish_reason : tool_calls
tool calls    : {"0": {"id": "call_scratch_1", "name": "get_weather",
                       "args": "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"}}
follow-up (assistant tool_calls + role:tool result accepted) -> 200

6. Image part (data: URL)
content       : I can see the image you sent.

7. n > 1 is refused with an OpenAI 400
raised        : BadRequestError
status        : 400
message       : Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'MCC serves one choice per
                request; n must be 1 or omitted.', 'type': 'invalid_request_error',
                'param': None, 'code': None}}

8. A wrong key is still rejected
raised        : AuthenticationError 401
```

### The upstream wire body MCC actually sent (request-detail API, MCC's own redaction)

For a non-streaming tool round trip with `reasoning_effort: "low"`,
`parallel_tool_calls: false` and a `role: "tool"` result:

```json
{
 "model": "fake-model",
 "reasoning_effort": "low",
 "max_tokens": 256,
 "stream": true,
 "stream_options": {"include_usage": true},
 "tool_choice": "auto",
 "messages": [
  {"role": "system",    "content": {"type": "text", "chars": 8}},
  {"role": "user",      "content": {"type": "text", "chars": 35}},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": {"type": "text", "chars": 0},
                        "tool_calls": [{"name": "get_weather"}]},
  {"role": "tool",      "content": {"type": "text", "chars": 13}}
 ],
 "tools": [{"name": "get_weather", "params": ["city"]}]
}
```

`response_shape` for that attempt: `content` 1 delta / 17 chars, `tool_calls`
3 deltas, `chunks: 7`, `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, usage keys including
`prompt_tokens_details` and `completion_tokens_details`.

The image request's body shows the part reached upstream as `image_url`
alongside the text part.

### Request log

```
endpoint = /v1/chat/completions | protocol = openai_chat | stream = False | status = success
params   = {"max_tokens": 256, "tools_count": 1,
            "tool_choice": {"type": "auto", "disable_parallel_tool_use": true}}
reasoning = control=default,effort=low
tool_calls = [{"name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Paris"}}]
headers.user-agent = OpenAI/Python 2.54.0
```

`stream = False` is the client's own intent, not the always-true internal one:
`build_capture` gained a `stream` override for exactly that, because the
Anthropic request every surface converts to is always streaming.

## Tests

New:

- `tests/core/openai_chat_completions/test_chat_input.py` — **22** tests over
  every request field in the table above, including both `image_url` forms, the
  tool-result coalescing, the `parallel_tool_calls` folding, `response_format`
  both ways, the `n` refusal, and the dropped-field trace row.
- `tests/core/openai_chat_completions/test_chat_sse.py` — **35** tests: text,
  thinking -> `reasoning_content`, two interleaved tool calls with incremental
  arguments and their own indices, every `finish_reason`, the usage chunk with
  cached and reasoning details, `[DONE]`, the `error` frame, pre-start vs
  post-start failure, source close on early exit, and non-stream assembly.
- `tests/api/test_openai_chat_completions.py` — **16** HTTP tests through the
  same `resolve_provider` seam the Responses tests use.
- `tests/contracts/test_proxy_auth_startup_policy.py` — **15** tests.
- `tests/cli/test_server_auth_guard.py` — **3** tests (refusal happens before
  `build_asgi_app` and before the port probe).

Extended, so the new surface is held to the contracts the other two are:
`tests/api/test_execution_failure_contract.py` (third arm on both
parametrisations plus three chat-specific terminal tests, pinning
`wire_api: "chat_completions"`), `tests/api/test_ordinary_error_phases.py`
(third tuple across all five parametrised tests),
`tests/core/test_protocol_model_ownership.py` (model ownership + three more
import orders), `tests/api/test_api.py` (probe methods),
`tests/cli/test_harness_registry.py` (every `HarnessProtocol` has a label — that
lookup is unguarded and would take the Coding agents page down),
`tests/contracts/test_import_boundaries.py` (the new package is facade-only).

Counts: **8322 passed**, 17 failed in the full run, of which **15 are the known
local baseline** (verified by running the same files on a detached worktree at
`fork/main`: identical 15) and 2 are installer PowerShell tests that pass alone
and fail only under a fully parallel run. jsdom alone (`-n 0`): **189 passed**.
`ruff format --check` clean over 1078 files, `ruff check src/ tests/ smoke/`
clean, `ty check` clean.

## Browser

Chrome DevTools MCP against the scratch dashboard, **zero console errors**.
Screenshots in `screenshots-chat-pr8/`:

1. `01-guide-openai-clients.png` — the new Guide section, in the TOC between
   "Point another CLI here" and "Search the web", with the base URL table, the
   two-shapes paragraph, the curl block (with its own Copy button) and the
   note about `n` and the dropped fields. `document.body.scrollWidth` is 8px
   under `window.innerWidth`, so no horizontal overflow.
2. `02-coding-agents-protocols.png` — 10 harness cards still render; the
   protocol rows read `Anthropic Messages (POST /v1/messages)` and
   `OpenAI Responses (POST /v1/responses)`, unchanged (no harness adopts the new
   protocol in this PR).
3. `03-requests-chat-completions-rows.png` — request rows for all three
   endpoints side by side.
4. `04-request-detail-protocol-openai-chat.png` — the detail pane showing
   `Endpoint /v1/chat/completions`, `Protocol openai_chat`, the reasoning policy,
   the params and the redacted request body.

The browser drive caught a real defect: the curl block's line continuations had
been eaten, joining it into one line. Fixed before the commit.

## Deviations from the brief

- **`response_format` is a system instruction, not a forced tool call.** The
  brief allowed "the nearest Anthropic mechanism or a clear 400". A forced-tool
  encoding is arguably nearer, but it changes `finish_reason` semantics and the
  whole streaming shape; an instruction carrying the schema verbatim is honest,
  cheap, and what every OpenAI-compatible proxy does. Unknown types still 400.
- **Small refactor outside the new package.** `core/openai_common/` was created
  for the error envelope, the failure-kind map, the Anthropic SSE reader and the
  token estimator, rather than copying ~150 lines into the new adapter.
  `core/openai_responses` keeps every one of those names importable, so its
  tests and its public surface are byte-identical in behaviour.
  `api/wire_surfaces.py` similarly replaces two hand-written path literals in
  `app.py` that would otherwise have had to be extended in two places.

## Residual risks

- **`status: cancelled` on some streamed rows.** A client that stops reading at
  `[DONE]` leaves the capture recording `cancelled` rather than `success`. This
  is **pre-existing and shared with `/v1/responses`** — verified on the same
  server in the same session, where a `/v1/responses` request recorded
  `cancelled` and a `/v1/messages` one recorded `success`. Not introduced here
  and not fixed here.
- **Clean truncation after a committed stream stays off** for this surface, as
  it is for Responses (`wire_api != "messages"` in `execution.py`). A stream that
  dies mid-answer ends with an `error` object rather than a clean `length`
  finish. Chat Completions *could* express that ending; choosing to is a
  behaviour change worth its own review.
- **`reasoning_tokens` is an estimate**, capped by the real `completion_tokens`.
  Anthropic reports one output count and never says how much of it was thinking.
- **No harness targets the new protocol yet.** `HarnessProtocol.OPENAI_CHAT_COMPLETIONS`
  exists and is labelled; Cline & co are PR 9.
- **`GET /v1/models` advertises ids with a slash in them** (`anthropic/lmstudio/…`).
  Unchanged by this PR, but a client with a strict model-id parser may struggle;
  every id the other two surfaces accept is accepted here.
- The live proof used a **fake** upstream gateway. No real provider credential
  was exercised for this surface.

## Action required for operators

An install that both listens beyond loopback (`HOST` other than `127.0.0.1` /
`localhost` / `::1`) **and** has an empty `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` will refuse to
start after this release. Set a token, or set `HOST=127.0.0.1`. The refusal
message names both. Installs created by `mcc-init` are unaffected: the shipped
template sets a token.

commit.message:
feat(api): serve OpenAI Chat Completions, and refuse to serve an unauthenticated proxy to the network

MCC accepted three inbound shapes and none of them was the one almost every
OpenAI-compatible client actually sends. Cline, Aider, Goose, Droid and every
IDE plugin that says "point me at an OpenAI base URL" speak
`POST /v1/chat/completions`; MCC answered 404, so the only way in was a
translating shim the user had to run themselves.

`POST /v1/chat/completions` now exists beside `/v1/messages` and
`/v1/responses`, built the way the Responses adapter was: a `core` package that
only translates, and a handler that hands the result to the same
`ModelRouter` -> `ProviderExecutor` every other surface uses. Routing, the
fallback chain, pause, reasoning gating, output budgets, wire capture, the
upstream ladder, the request log, analytics and the optimizer rules therefore
apply to all three doors identically -- a request costs and behaves the same
whichever one it arrives through, which is the only claim that makes a third
surface worth having.

Inbound: `messages` with `system`/`developer` roles, string and multi-part
content, `image_url` as both a base64 data URL and an http reference,
`tools`/`tool_choice`/`parallel_tool_calls` (Anthropic keeps the last of those
inside `tool_choice`, so the two are converted together), `tool` role results
coalesced into one Anthropic user turn, `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens`,
`temperature`/`top_p`/`stop`, `reasoning_effort` preserved as a named effort for
the routing layer to price, and `response_format` mapped to the nearest
Anthropic mechanism -- an instruction carrying the JSON Schema verbatim, since
Anthropic has no server-enforced JSON mode. `n` above 1 is refused with a 400
rather than served quietly as one choice; `seed`, `logprobs` and the two
penalties have no equivalent upstream and are dropped with a trace row rather
than silently.

Outbound: `chat.completion.chunk` frames with `delta.content`,
`delta.reasoning_content` (plus `delta.reasoning`, one key, for the other
client family), `delta.tool_calls` indexed by tool call rather than by Anthropic
block with incremental `arguments`, `finish_reason` translated from
`stop_reason`, a choiceless usage chunk when `stream_options.include_usage` asks
for one, and `[DONE]`. Non-streaming assembles that same internal stream into
one `chat.completion` at the API boundary, exactly as `/v1/messages` does; there
is no second pipeline to drift. `prompt_tokens` includes what the cache served
and reports it under `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, because Anthropic's
`input_tokens` excludes it and a straight rename would under-report the prompt
of most requests a coding agent makes. A failure after the first frame is an
`error` object inside the body then `[DONE]` -- what the OpenAI SDK stream
readers raise on -- rather than a bare terminator that reads as an empty answer.

The error envelope and the failure-kind mapping the two OpenAI surfaces share
moved to `core/openai_common`, with the Anthropic SSE reader and the token
estimator; `core/openai_responses` keeps them importable and is otherwise
untouched. `api/wire_surfaces.py` now owns the path-to-surface map that two
error boundaries in `app.py` were each answering with their own literal.

The auth fail-open, second. `require_proxy_auth` returns early when
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is empty and `HOST` defaults to `0.0.0.0`, so the
defaults together are an open proxy on the LAN spending the operator's provider
credits, and no request-time check can catch it because the request-time check
is the one that returns early. `mcc-server` now refuses to start in exactly that
combination, before the socket is bound, naming both variables and the card that
edits them. A loopback bind with no token still runs: that is a deliberate
single-machine setup. The compare itself is unchanged. The default install is
not affected -- `mcc-init` writes `.env.example`, whose token is populated --
and a contract test pins that, along with the page and card the message names
against the shipped `admin.js`.

Also: `HarnessProtocol.OPENAI_CHAT_COMPLETIONS` and its label, so the Coding
agents page can name the surface when a harness adopts it (none does here); a
Guide section giving the base URL, the header and `GET /v1/models`; and
`protocol="openai_chat"` in the request log, with the client's own `stream`
intent recorded rather than the always-true internal one.
